operations.title: Who am I
operations.description: Show the connected OpenSEO account, server mode, token scopes, and remaining credits. Use it when the user asks to check their account, connection, or credit balance. Sets up billing on a new hosted account's first call. Uses no credits.

operations.title: List projects
operations.description: List the user's projects with their id, name, domain, and default market. Use it whenever another OpenSEO tool needs a projectId: pass the project's id. Tools fall back to the project's default market when a call omits location or language. Uses no credits. When there is no project yet, use create_project.

operations.title: Create project
operations.description: Create a project in the user's organization. Provide a name, and optionally a domain and a default market (locationCode and languageCode; a languageCode requires a locationCode). Pass the returned id as projectId to other OpenSEO tools. Uses no credits. Call list_projects first to avoid creating a duplicate.

domain.description: Optional root domain for the project, e.g. "example.com" (host only, no scheme or path). Sets the default target for domain, backlink, and rank tools.

locationCode.description: Optional DataForSEO location code for the project's default market (e.g. 2840 = United States, 2504 = Morocco). Falls back to the organization default when omitted.

languageCode.description: Optional language code (e.g. "en", "fr"). Requires locationCode; derived from the location when omitted.

operations.title: Research project website
operations.description: Research a project's website to draft its missing setup: brand name, domain, business overview, competitors, and Prompt Research topics. Saved values are reused, and competitors are searched for only when none are saved; preserveCompetitors=true means the saved list is kept and competitors is empty, and a researched list is also empty if live search was unavailable. Returns five suggested topics with five prompts each, plus up to fifteen suggested keywords, only when research keywords are missing. Needs a positive credit balance to start, then bills actual model and search costs, even if that makes the balance negative. Results are drafts, not saved or tracked: review them with the user, then save with save_project_website_setup.

operations.title: Save reviewed website setup
operations.description: Save a website setup drafted by research_project_website or complete_ai_research_setup once the user confirms it: fills the project's missing website domain, business overview, and competitors. name sets the brand name AI visibility looks for in answers, so confirm it with the user too. Existing project values and competitor lists are never overwritten; a new competitor list can include manual additions the user reviewed. Pass suggestedTopics and suggestedKeywords from the research: when research keywords are missing they fill them (saved keywords are kept, the response warns that the list was ignored, and update_ai_research_keywords changes them), and the first three topics start weekly AI tracking, with its first paid check about a week later, unless the project already tracks prompts. Saving uses no credits and starts no answer collection. For explicit edits to saved context, use update_project_context.

name.description: A succinct topic name, at most five words

operations.title: Get project context
operations.description: Read a project's shared memory: business overview, current goal, positioning, writing preferences, custom sections, competitors, key pages, and the recent research log. Call it before SEO work to ground the work in what the user already told OpenSEO, and check the research log before buying the same research again. Uses no credits. To fill sections listed as missing, use update_project_context.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

operations.title: Update project context
operations.description: Add, edit, or delete entries in a project's shared memory, which the app, SAM, and other agents all read. Sections are prose (~4,000 characters max), competitors and key pages are curated shortlists (100 max each), and appendResearchLog records research already bought. Confirm facts with the user before storing them. Uses no credits. Call get_project_context first to find entries to remove; for report templates, use save_report_template.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

customSection.description: Lowercase letters and digits separated by hyphens, e.g. 'launch-plan'. No underscores or spaces. Use the same slug to edit or delete the section.

deleteCustomSection.description: Lowercase letters and digits separated by hyphens, e.g. 'launch-plan'. No underscores or spaces. Use the same slug to edit or delete the section.

updates.description: Patch ops, applied in order. Set the name AI visibility looks for in answers with {brandName: "Acme"}, after the user confirms it; an empty string goes back to the project name. Clear a standard section with {section: "current_goal", content: ""}; delete a custom section with {deleteCustomSection: "slug"}; removeCompetitors takes domains, removeKeyPages takes URLs, and removeResearchLog takes entry IDs from the project context. Adds upsert by domain/url; research-log entries are date-stamped by the server.

operations.title: List saved keywords
operations.description: List the keywords saved to a project, with cached search volume, difficulty, CPC, and tags when available. Filter by tag when the user asks for a saved segment; multiple tags match any of them. Uses no credits. To delete rows, pass their saved-keyword IDs to remove_saved_keywords; for fresh metrics, use get_keyword_metrics.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

tags.description: Optional tag-name filters. Multiple tags match ANY tag.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 100.

operations.title: Remove saved keywords
operations.description: Permanently delete keywords from a project's saved-keywords list by their saved-keyword ID from list_saved_keywords. Missing, foreign-project, and repeated IDs are ignored. Uses no credits. This does not change rank tracking: for that, use remove_rank_tracking_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

savedKeywordIds.description: Saved-keyword row IDs to delete. Use the `id` values returned by list_saved_keywords.

operations.title: Get suggested keywords
operations.description: Suggest up to 10 short seed keywords to research next: Search Console searches where the site's best page ranks 4–6 (close to the top 3) or 11–20 (close to page 1), then the project's saved topics. Use it when the user asks what to research or where to start. Search Console suggestions need a connected property. Uses no credits. Pass the suggestions to research_keywords as seeds.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

operations.title: Research keywords (bulk)
operations.description: Find keyword ideas for 1-5 seed keywords in one call, each with search volume, keyword difficulty, and CPC. Use it to learn what people search for around a topic. One bad seed won't fail the batch. Costs ~54 credits per seed at the default result limit and ~110 at 500; an obscure seed's fallback lookup adds ~40-95, and countries served from Google Ads data cost a flat ~96, without difficulty or intent. For metrics on keywords you already have, use get_keyword_metrics; for seeds to start from, use get_suggested_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

seed.description: Seed keyword to research. Use * as a wildcard for any word or words: "best * for dogs" returns only keywords matching that pattern (e.g. "best flea treatment for dogs"), one request at about the same cost. Wildcards need at least one other word and are unavailable for countries served from Google Ads data.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

locationName.description: Optional city, county, or region inside the seed's country, for local search volume. Call search_serp_locations first and pass its locationName verbatim. Volume, CPC, and competition then come from Google Ads for that area; keyword ideas, KD, and intent stay national. Adds ~116 credits per seed.

seeds.description: 1-5 seed keywords. Each seed is researched independently and returns related keywords with volume/difficulty/CPC. Bulk-friendly — prefer this over multiple single-seed calls.

resultLimit.description: Max keywords returned per seed. Defaults to 150. Auto mode blends two sources; duplicate keywords across sources appear once.

includeClickstreamData.description: Refine search volumes with clickstream data, which disaggregates Google Ads' grouped close-variant volumes (plurals/misspellings). DOUBLES the credit cost of each seed. Default false (standard Google-Ads-derived volumes). No effect for countries served from Google Ads data.

groupKeywords.description: Include similar keyword variants that can share volume, CPC, and competition. Default false returns only core keywords (DataForSEO ignore_synonyms=true). True includes variants (ignore_synonyms=false). This filters keywords, not metric estimates. Do not sum shared volumes. No effect for countries served from Google Ads data.

operations.title: Save keywords
operations.description: Save keywords to a project's saved-keywords list, optionally with metrics and tags. Re-saving an existing keyword is a no-op. Tags are appended by default; tagMode=replace removes the keywords' existing tags first, which is useful for regrouping keywords into page or topic clusters. Ask the user for confirmation before applying or replacing tags broadly. Uses no credits. To track rankings for keywords, use add_rank_tracking_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

metrics.description: Optional metrics for the saved keywords. Copy keyword, searchVolume, keywordDifficulty, cpc, competition, and intent from research_keywords or get_keyword_metrics rows. monthlySearches is optional. Match each metric using its keyword field.

tags.description: Optional tags to attach to every saved keyword. Ask the user for explicit confirmation before using this, especially when saving many keywords or creating new tag names.

tagMode.description: How to apply tags. Defaults to append. Use replace to remove existing tags from these saved keywords before applying the provided tags.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

operations.title: Get keyword metrics
operations.description: Get search volume, keyword difficulty (KD), search intent, CPC, competition, and monthly trends for up to 700 keywords you already have. Use it to score candidate or known keywords, including Search Console striking-distance queries, by real demand and ranking difficulty. For countries served from Google Ads data (such as Iceland), KD and intent are null. Uses credits. To find new keyword ideas from a seed, use research_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

includeMonthlyTrends.description: Include monthly search-volume trend rows. Defaults to true.

includeClickstreamData.description: Refine search volumes with clickstream data, which disaggregates Google Ads' grouped close-variant volumes (plurals/misspellings). DOUBLES the credit cost of the call. Default false. No effect for countries served from Google Ads data.

sortBy.description: Sort order for returned rows. Defaults to search_volume.

operations.title: Get domain overview
operations.description: Estimate a website's monthly organic search traffic and how many keywords it ranks for. Use it first when researching a domain, the user's own or a competitor's. Costs ~100-300 credits; cached for 12 hours per domain. For the keywords it ranks for, use get_domain_keyword_suggestions; for backlinks, use get_backlinks_overview.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

scope.description: Research scope: 'domain' (hostname without subdomains), 'subdomains' (hostname plus all subdomains), 'subfolder' (path and its children), or 'exact_url' (one page). Defaults to 'subdomains' for root inputs and 'subfolder' when the input has a path. Overview metrics always cover the hostname plus subdomains; narrower scopes are labeled accordingly — use get_ranked_keywords with a scope for scoped keyword data.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

operations.title: Get domain keyword opportunities
operations.description: List the organic keywords a domain ranks for, with position and available metrics. Use it after get_domain_overview for a competitor's or reference domain's keyword opportunities. Costs ~100-300 credits; cached for 12 hours. To filter by rank, search volume, or brand terms, use get_ranked_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

domain.description: Competitor or reference domain or URL to extract keywords from.

scope.description: Research scope: 'domain' (hostname without subdomains), 'subdomains' (hostname plus all subdomains), 'subfolder' (path and its children), or 'exact_url' (one page). Defaults to 'subdomains' for root inputs and 'subfolder' when the input has a path.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

operations.title: Get ranked keywords
operations.description: List the keywords a domain or page ranks for in one country, each with its ranking URL, rank, search volume, CPC, intent, and estimated traffic. Use it as evidence for strategy: which keywords and pages earn a site its search traffic. Filter by maxRank, minSearchVolume, or excludeBrandTerms. Uses credits. For a site's total traffic and keyword count, use get_domain_overview.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

target.description: Domain (no protocol/www) or absolute page URL to list ranked keywords for.

scope.description: Research scope: 'domain' (hostname without subdomains), 'subdomains' (hostname plus all subdomains), 'subfolder' (path and its children), or 'exact_url' (one page). Defaults to 'subdomains' for root inputs and 'subfolder' when the input has a path.

market.description: Legacy US selector. Prefer locationCode/languageCode for any Labs market. Explicit locationCode takes precedence; otherwise omitted = the project's default market.

country.description: Country selector. Only the United States can be selected explicitly.

locationCode.description: Country-level DataForSEO Labs location code. Defaults to the project's market; takes precedence over the legacy market object.

languageCode.description: Language for locationCode. Defaults to that location's primary language when locationCode overrides the project market.

resultTypes.description: SERP result types to include. Defaults to organic and paid.

minSearchVolume.description: Only return keywords with at least this monthly search volume.

maxRank.description: Only return keywords ranking at this position or better.

excludeBrandTerms.description: Exclude keywords containing any of these brand terms.

sortBy.description: Sort order for returned rows. Defaults to search_volume.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (1-100). Defaults to 50.

operations.title: Get backlinks overview
operations.description: Summarize the backlink profile of a domain or page: total backlinks, referring domains, and top referring domains. Bare domains include subdomains by default; pass scope 'domain' to exclude them. Trend data always includes subdomains. Costs ~50 credits for a domain and ~25 for a single page. Self-hosted deployments need the Backlinks API enabled on their DataForSEO account. For the individual links, use get_backlinks_profile.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

target.description: Domain or URL to analyze (e.g. 'example.com' or 'https://example.com/blog').

scope.description: Research scope: 'domain' (hostname without subdomains), 'subdomains' (hostname plus all subdomains), 'subfolder' (path and its children), or 'exact_url' (one page). Defaults to 'subdomains' for root inputs and 'subfolder' when the input has a path. 'page' is a deprecated alias of 'exact_url'. Subfolder counts are computed from filtered backlink totals; rank, trends, and the referring-domains breakdown are unavailable for subfolders.

hideSpam.description: Filter out spammy referring domains. Defaults to true.

operations.title: Get backlinks profile
operations.description: List the individual backlinks of a domain or page: linking and target URLs, anchors, dofollow or nofollow, authority and spam signals, and lost or broken status. Supports filters, sorting, pagination, and a mode of one_per_domain (the default) or as_is. Costs ~30 credits per page of rows. Self-hosted deployments need the Backlinks API enabled on their DataForSEO account. For totals and top referring domains, use get_backlinks_overview.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

target.description: Domain or URL to analyze (e.g. 'example.com' or 'https://example.com/blog').

scope.description: Research scope: 'domain' (hostname without subdomains), 'subdomains' (hostname plus all subdomains), 'subfolder' (path and its children), or 'exact_url' (one page). Defaults to 'subdomains' for root inputs and 'subfolder' when the input has a path. 'page' is a deprecated alias of 'exact_url'. Subfolder counts are computed from filtered backlink totals; rank, trends, and the referring-domains breakdown are unavailable for subfolders.

pageSize.description: Rows per page. Allowed values: 50, 100, or 200.

filters.description: Backlink row filters: include/exclude source URL terms, authority/spam ranges, dofollow/nofollow, lost/broken visibility, or exact domainFrom.

mode.description: DataForSEO backlink grouping: one_per_domain returns each referring domain's strongest link; as_is returns individual backlink rows.

hideSpam.description: Hide backlinks with Spam scores of 40 or higher. Defaults to true. Unknown scores remain visible. This is a heuristic, not a judgment about a link. Set false to inspect all matching links. True leaves six user filter conditions (two for subfolders); false allows eight (four for subfolders). Each include/exclude term and numeric bound counts separately.

operations.title: Get Google SERP results
operations.description: Get live Google organic search results for 1-10 keywords. Use it to see who ranks for a query, verify competitors, compare SERPs across keywords, or gather source URLs before content planning. Google serves automated readers pages that vary, so each keyword is read 3 times and merged into one row per site; expect 10-30 seconds. Quote bestPosition as a site's position: `rank` only numbers the merged rows, and a site with seenIn 1 is weak evidence. `url` can be a google.com/goto redirect that a plain fetch won't follow; `domain` is the reliable field, and finalUrls returns the page URLs for a job that can wait a few minutes. Costs ~5 credits per keyword at the default depth 10, and each additional 10 of depth adds ~3.5. Repeating the same call within 12 hours returns the same reads at no charge, so if a response is lost or a keyword is still running, wait a minute and repeat it. Per-keyword errors don't fail the batch. For a site's position over time, use get_rank_tracker or get_search_console_performance.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

keyword.description: Search query to fetch the SERP for.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

locationName.description: Optional city, county, or region inside the query's country, for a local SERP. Call search_serp_locations first and pass its locationName verbatim. Same price as a national SERP.

device.description: Device to fetch the SERP for, default desktop. Use mobile to compare against a mobile rank tracker. Same price.

queries.description: 1-10 queries. Bulk-friendly — prefer this over multiple single-query calls.

depth.description: How many Google results to read per keyword — a multiple of 10 from 10 to 100, default 10 (page 1). Merging the reads usually returns more sites than this. Google has no offset, so a deeper read re-fetches the top too: each additional 10 adds ~3.5 credits per keyword. Only raise it when you need ranks past page 1.

finalUrls.description: Set true to get each result's page URL instead of a google.com/goto redirect. The search then takes a few minutes instead of seconds: the first call starts it and answers that it is still running, and the same call again 2-3 minutes later returns the results at no extra charge. For batch jobs, not while someone waits. Costs about half the credits.

operations.title: Search SERP locations
operations.description: Find the exact location name of a city, county, or region in a country, for local searches. Returns up to 50 matches. Uses no credits. Pass the chosen locationName verbatim to create_rank_tracker for local rank tracking, to get_serp_results for a local SERP, or to research_keywords for local search volume.

operations.title: Find SERP competitors
operations.description: Find the domains that compete in Google results for a set of 1-100 keywords, sorted by visibility, estimated traffic, average position, or keyword count. Use it to learn who a site's real search competitors are for a topic. Works on a country-level market, not radius-based local SEO. Uses credits. For local competitors near a place, use search_local_businesses; for who ranks on one keyword, use get_serp_results.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

market.description: Legacy US selector. Prefer locationCode/languageCode for any Labs market. Explicit locationCode takes precedence; otherwise omitted = the project's default market.

country.description: Country selector. Only the United States can be selected explicitly.

locationCode.description: Country-level DataForSEO Labs location code. Defaults to the project's market; takes precedence over the legacy market object.

languageCode.description: Language for locationCode. Defaults to that location's primary language when locationCode overrides the project market.

resultTypes.description: SERP result types to include. Defaults to organic and local_pack.

excludeDomains.description: Domains to exclude from results (e.g. the user's own site).

includeSubdomains.description: Count subdomains as part of the same competitor domain.

sortBy.description: Sort order for returned competitors. Defaults to visibility.

limit.description: Maximum competitors to return (1-100). Defaults to 50.

operations.title: Get AI visibility tracker
operations.description: Read a project's AI visibility tracking setup: topics, exact prompts, the brand and competitors answers are matched against, engine and country capabilities, and recent runs. Returns configured=false when no tracker exists. Uses no credits and never starts a check. To change the setup, use save_ai_visibility_tracker; for a run's findings, use get_ai_visibility_results.

operations.title: Save AI visibility tracker
operations.description: Create or update AI visibility tracking in bulk: prompts, their topics, engines, country, and language. Call get_ai_visibility_tracker first and edit prompts by ID; pause or archive a topic by pausing or archiving each of its prompts. Do not rewrite the customer's prompts without direction. Brand and competitors come from project context: change them with update_project_context. Saving uses no credits. A new tracker starts on a weekly schedule, with its first paid check about a week later; estimate_ai_visibility_cost prices the checks, and set_ai_visibility_schedule pauses them.

locationCode.description: Country for collection, as a DataForSEO location code from the project market list (2840 = United States). A new tracker defaults to the project's market. Check capabilities for countries an engine cannot use.

languageCode.description: Language for collection. Omit when changing country to use that country's default language.

id.description: Existing prompt ID when editing or pausing. Omit for a new prompt. Changing an existing prompt's text archives it and adds the new text as a new prompt, so earlier answers keep their exact prompt.

text.description: Exact customer prompt or keyword, up to 2,000 characters; casing is preserved. Do not expand or rewrite without the user's direction.

topic.description: Topic name that groups the prompt. New prompts default to General; edits without a topic keep the saved topic. Set it on an existing prompt to move the prompt; to rename a topic, move every prompt in it.

operations.title: Explore an AI prompt
operations.description: Ask one prompt in ChatGPT, or compare answers from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity. Returns answer text, citations, search queries, brand mentions, and per-model errors. Use it for a one-off look at how AI answers a question. Costs credits for actual model usage per uncached model, and web search may make one more paid attempt if the first answer did not search; cached answers are free for seven days. Requires a paid plan on hosted OpenSEO. For consumer-site observations and recurring monitoring, use the AI visibility tracking tools, starting with get_ai_visibility_tracker.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

prompt.description: The exact question to ask, up to 500 characters. Preserve the user's wording.

models.description: Models to query: chat_gpt, claude, gemini, perplexity. Defaults to ChatGPT only. Supply a list to compare selected models; each uncached model uses credits.

highlightBrand.description: Optional brand to highlight in answer text and citations. Does not change the prompt sent to the models.

webSearch.description: Allow web search, default true. Answers report whether the model actually searched; permission does not guarantee citations.

webSearchCountryCode.description: Optional two-letter web-search country code. Omit to use the project's country, or no country preference when a selected model cannot use it. Gemini always answers without a country. A country you name returns per-model errors for other models that cannot use it, without a paid call.

operations.title: Generate AI tracking prompts
operations.description: Generate editable topic and prompt suggestions for AI tracking from the project's shared context. Supply topic to add prompts to a saved topic or to name a new one, or omit it for a new topic the model names. Saved prompts and excludePrompts drafts are left out. Costs credits for one model call. Nothing is saved or collected: review the suggestions, then save them through save_ai_visibility_tracker with the returned topic. For questions people already ask about a keyword, use research_ai_visibility_prompts.

topic.description: A saved topic to add prompts to, or a new topic name. Omit to let the model name a new topic.

operations.title: Research AI prompts
operations.description: Find questions people ask about a keyword, with ChatGPT's answer to each, the sources it cited, and whether the project's domain is cited or its brand mentioned. US English data only. The questions come from a database built mostly from Google "People also ask" questions; they are not logged ChatGPT prompts, and nobody can see real ChatGPT prompt volume. A model keeps only the questions that use the keyword in the business's sense, so niche keywords may return few prompts. The most common questions come first. Costs credits for one prompt search and one relevance check per keyword, cached for 24 hours. Requires a paid plan on hosted OpenSEO. Nothing is saved or collected: save picked prompts with source prompt_research through save_ai_visibility_tracker. For new prompt ideas written from project context, use generate_ai_visibility_prompts.

keyword.description: A short head term such as a tracker topic name. Exact multi-word phrases return few prompts.

variants.description: Near-duplicate prompts merged into this one.

operations.title: Complete AI research setup
operations.description: Set up Prompt Research keywords for a project that has a saved website. Returns keywords, status, and review. Research uses OpenSEO credits: it sends project context to an external model and reads websites or searches for competitors when needed. An existing tracker, a running setup, or a setup awaiting review is returned without restarting research, and saved context and keywords are reused. When no tracker exists, saving the setup also creates three topics with five prompts each and turns on weekly paid AI checks, first due about a week later; no answer check starts immediately. For status=running, call again after about 20 seconds. For status=review, review the proposed setup with the user, then save it through save_project_website_setup, preserving saved competitors when review.preserveCompetitors=true. To change keywords that are already saved, use update_ai_research_keywords.

operations.title: Update Prompt Research keywords
operations.description: Edit a project's saved Prompt Research keywords, the shortcuts listed on the Prompt Research page: remove takes keywords off the list and add puts new ones on it, so one call swaps keywords. Call it with neither to read the list. Returns keywords, the list Prompt Research now shows, and trackedTopics, the tracker topics among them. Tracked topics are always listed; change those with save_ai_visibility_tracker. Uses no credits and starts no research.

remove.description: Saved keywords to take off the list. Case and spacing don't matter.

add.description: Keywords to put at the top of the list, such as replacements for the removed ones.

operations.title: Estimate AI visibility cost
operations.description: Estimate what AI visibility checks cost, without collecting answers: one scheduled check, a one-off check, and a month of a daily, weekly, or monthly schedule. Pass patch to price proposed settings, or promptIds to price only those prompts. costUsd prices each scheduled check; runNowCostUsd prices a one-off check, which collects live answers sooner at a higher price. Uses no credits. To run a one-off check, pass runNowCostUsd to run_ai_visibility_check as maxCostUsd.

patch.description: Optional proposed changes to estimate before saving.

languageCode.description: Language for collection. Omit when changing country to use that country's default language.

id.description: Existing prompt ID when editing or pausing. Omit for a new prompt. Changing an existing prompt's text archives it and adds the new text as a new prompt, so earlier answers keep their exact prompt.

topic.description: Topic name that groups the prompt. New prompts default to General; edits without a topic keep the saved topic. Set it on an existing prompt to move the prompt; to rename a topic, move every prompt in it.

operations.title: Set AI visibility schedule
operations.description: Turn AI visibility tracking on at a daily, weekly, or monthly cadence, change the cadence or run time, or pause future checks. An enabled schedule spends credits on every check, and checks stop when credits run out. The first enable queues one baseline check and returns its run: read that run instead of buying another check. Pausing lets a running check finish. For what a check costs, use estimate_ai_visibility_cost; for a one-off check now, use run_ai_visibility_check.

operations.title: Run AI visibility check
operations.description: Start a one-off paid AI visibility check now, leaving the schedule unchanged. It collects live answers, about 15 a minute: a few prompts finish within minutes, and 300 prompts on six engines (1,800 answers) take about 2 hours. maxCostUsd is a spending ceiling: pass runNowCostUsd from estimate_ai_visibility_cost, and the check is refused if it now costs more. Only one check runs per project at a time. Returns a run immediately: follow it with get_ai_visibility_run, and never call this tool again to poll.

operations.title: Get AI visibility run
operations.description: Check the progress of an AI visibility check: completed, failed, and pending answer counts, and how long to wait before polling again. This only reads progress; the check advances on its own. Uses no credits. When the run has finished, read it with get_ai_visibility_results.

operations.title: Get AI visibility results
operations.description: Read how often the brand and its competitors appear in AI answers for one tracking run: prompt and engine observations, plus brand comparison counts. For a normal review make one run-wide call with no filters (runId, topic, engines, and promptId null, competitorGap false): never enumerate every engine or prompt, and pass engines to filter to a few in a single call. Defaults to neutral prompts in the latest baseline or scheduled run, excluding manual checks; pass a manual run's runId to read it, and branded=all to include branded diagnostics. Derive competitor gaps from the returned rows, or make a separate competitorGap=true query. Uses no credits. Next, read get_ai_visibility_sources once with the returned runId, and inspect 2-3 full answers by passing observation IDs to get_ai_visibility_answer.

topic.description: Omit or null for all topics in the run. Filter by an exact saved topic name only when requested; do not use the string all.

engines.description: Omit or null for all engines in one call. Provide one or more engines for an explicitly requested subset, or an empty array for no engines. Do not make separate calls for each engine or use the string all.

It never collects a new answer or fetches the cited pages. Uses no credits. Long answers are truncated: for the full text, use export_ai_visibility_data.

Defaults to neutral prompts; pass branded=all to include branded diagnostics. A competitorGap=true query is a separate subset and must be labeled as one; coverage describes the run before the gap filter, so check appliedFilters. Uses no credits, and never crawls URLs or collects answers. For the answers behind a source, pass its observation IDs to get_ai_visibility_answer.

operations.title: Get AI visibility trend
operations.description: Check whether AI visibility is improving or declining: compares the latest N days with the N days before, using neutral prompts from finished runs. Read comparison before claiming movement: only comparable reports a change; incomplete (under 90% collection), scope_changed, no_previous, and no_data do not. Rates average only the prompt, engine, and market cells collected in both periods, and failed or no-answer collections count as coverage, never as lost visibility. Uses no credits. operations.description: Export stored AI visibility observations, with full answers, as a private CSV or JSON download for the requested scope. Returns an expiring link, not a large chat payload. operations.title: Create rank tracker
operations.description: Create a rank tracker for a project. The domain and market default to the project's; devices default to mobile, search depth to 40, and schedule to manual. For local (city-level) tracking, call search_serp_locations first and pass its locationName verbatim. Creating an empty tracker uses no credits and starts no check, but daily, weekly, and monthly trackers spend credits once keywords are added. Call get_rank_tracker first to avoid duplicates, and estimate_rank_tracker_cost before adding keywords to a scheduled tracker or starting a check.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

domain.description: Domain to track. Defaults to the project's domain. Accepts a hostname or URL and stores the normalized hostname.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO country location code (e.g. 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom). Defaults to the project's default market (see list_projects; editable in project settings). See dataforseo.com/help-center/locations. Some countries (e.g. Iceland, 2352) are served from Google Ads data: keyword volume/CPC/trends work, but keyword difficulty, search intent, and domain analytics are unavailable.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

locationName.description: Exact DataForSEO location name for local rank tracking, e.g. "Catonsville,Maryland,United States". Must come from search_serp_locations; free-form names like "Catonsville, MD" are rejected.

devices.description: Devices to track. Defaults to mobile.

serpDepth.description: Number of Google results to inspect. Defaults to 40.

scheduleInterval.description: Check schedule. Defaults to manual so creating a tracker cannot cause future credit spend. Scheduled checks may use credits later.

scheduleTime.description: When scheduled checks run. Pass the user's timeZone with it so their local time is converted for you; the schedule is then fixed in UTC and shifts an hour when their clocks change. Omit it unless the user asks for a specific time: the default spreads checks across quiet hours. Daily runs at this time every day, weekly on the given weekday, monthly at this time on the last day of the month. Checks start within about 15 minutes of the chosen time. Not valid with a manual schedule.

weekday.description: Day of week, 0 = Sunday. Required for weekly schedules, ignored by the others.

timeZone.description: IANA timezone the weekday, hour, and minute are in, e.g. "America/New_York". Defaults to UTC.

operations.title: Get rank tracker
operations.description: Read a project's rank trackers and their latest Google positions. Without trackerId, lists every tracker in the project. With trackerId, returns its config and a page of the latest keyword positions, pinned keywords first, each with the trackingKeywordId used for removals and pins and a googleSerpUrl that opens a live Google search for the keyword in its market; use offset and limit for more keywords. lastCheckedAt shows how fresh a position is. A null position means the domain was not found in the results the check returned, which can be fewer than serpDepth, so it does not prove the domain ranks below serpDepth. Uses no credits. When no tracker exists, use create_rank_tracker; to manage one, use add_rank_tracking_keywords, remove_rank_tracking_keywords, pin_rank_tracking_keywords, or run_rank_tracker; for positions over time, use get_rank_history.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

trackerId.description: Rank tracker config ID. If omitted, lists all rank trackers in the project.

offset.description: Keyword row offset when trackerId is provided. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Keyword rows per page when trackerId is provided. Defaults to 100. Lower this if the text is truncated.

operations.title: Get rank history
operations.description: Read the position history of a rank tracker's keywords over its latest completed checks (up to 26), newest first, for one device. A null position (— in text) means the domain was not found in the results that check returned; `checked: false` (not checked in text) means the check got no result for the keyword, so it says nothing about the position. Checks that only re-ran some keywords are left out. Uses no credits. Call get_rank_tracker first for the trackerId and trackingKeywordId values.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

trackerId.description: Rank tracker config ID from get_rank_tracker.

device.description: Device to read. Defaults to desktop, or mobile for a mobile-only tracker.

runs.description: How many of the latest completed checks to return. Defaults to 12.

trackingKeywordId.description: Only return this keyword's history. IDs come from get_rank_tracker.

limit.description: Keyword rows per page. Defaults to 100. Lower this if the text is truncated.

operations.title: Add rank tracking keywords
operations.description: Add keywords to an existing rank tracker. It also fetches search volume, difficulty, and CPC for the tracker's keywords, which uses credits like get_keyword_metrics. It starts no check, but a scheduled tracker will spend credits on future recurring public Google searches. For a scheduled tracker, call estimate_rank_tracker_cost with additionalKeywords, show the recurring estimate to the user, and pass the approved per-check estimate as maxEstimatedScheduledCheckCredits. Existing and repeated keywords are skipped. To check positions now, use run_rank_tracker.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

keywords.description: Keywords to track. Existing and repeated keywords are skipped.

matchCase.description: Track the keywords exactly as typed instead of lowercasing them. Defaults to false. Use for brand names where Google's results differ by capitalization; a cased keyword is tracked and billed separately from its lowercase form.

maxEstimatedScheduledCheckCredits.description: Most credits per scheduled check, including retries, that the user approved after seeing estimate_rank_tracker_cost with additionalKeywords. Required for scheduled trackers.

operations.title: Remove rank tracking keywords
operations.description: Stop tracking keywords in a rank tracker by their trackingKeywordId from get_rank_tracker. Historical snapshots are kept. Missing, stale, foreign, and repeated IDs are ignored. Uses no credits. This does not change the saved-keywords list: for that, use remove_saved_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

keywordIds.description: Tracking keyword IDs to remove. Use `trackingKeywordId` values returned by get_rank_tracker.

operations.title: Pin rank tracking keywords
operations.description: Pin or unpin tracked keywords by their trackingKeywordId from get_rank_tracker. Pinned keywords stay at the top of the tracker's keyword table for everyone in the project, and get_rank_tracker lists them first. Missing, stale, foreign, and repeated IDs are ignored. Uses no credits.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

keywordIds.description: Tracking keyword IDs to pin or unpin. Use `trackingKeywordId` values returned by get_rank_tracker.

pinned.description: true pins the keywords to the top. false unpins them.

operations.title: Estimate rank tracker cost
operations.description: Estimate what a rank tracker check costs, without spending credits or starting a check. The estimate is the most a check can cost: two reads of every keyword and device. Most get one read, so a check usually costs a little over half the estimate. It covers one run_rank_tracker check; for a scheduled tracker, the response adds the per-check and approximate monthly cost. Pass additionalKeywords to price the tracker after adding keywords. Pass the estimate the user approves as maxCostCredits to run_rank_tracker, or as maxEstimatedScheduledCheckCredits to add_rank_tracking_keywords.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

additionalKeywordCount.description: Number of keywords you plan to add, priced as plain keywords. Prefer additionalKeywords when you know them.

additionalKeywords.description: Keywords you plan to add. Include these before adding to a scheduled tracker so the response projects its recurring per-check and monthly cost; keywords with search operators such as site: cost 5x. Overrides additionalKeywordCount.

operations.title: Run rank tracker
operations.description: Start a rank check now for every keyword and device in a tracker. This spends credits: call estimate_rank_tracker_cost, show the estimate to the user, and pass the approved credit amount as maxCostCredits; a fresh estimate above that ceiling is rejected. Hosted accounts need a paid plan. If a check is already running, its run ID is reported without starting or charging another. The schedule is unchanged. The check runs in the background: poll get_rank_tracker for the updated positions.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

maxCostCredits.description: Maximum credits the user approved after seeing estimate_rank_tracker_cost. The run is rejected if its fresh estimate is higher.

operations.title: Search local businesses
operations.description: Search local business listings near a coordinate, with optional category, rating, review-count, and claimed-status filters. Use it to discover businesses you cannot name yet: local candidates, nearby competitors, or unclaimed listings. Uses credits. When you already know the business, use get_business_profile instead: it returns the full profile for less than half the credits, so it is also the cheap way to check whether a Google Business Profile exists. For Google Maps rankings, use get_local_serp_results or get_local_rank_grid.

query.description: Text the business name must contain, such as a trade word. For a business type, use categories.

radiusKm.description: Search radius around the center, in whole kilometers (fractions are rounded).

near.description: Coordinate and radius to search around.

minRating.description: Only return businesses rated at least this (1-5).

minReviews.description: Only return businesses with at least this many Google reviews.

isClaimed.description: Filter by whether the listing is claimed by its owner. false surfaces unclaimed listings (outreach prospects).

sortBy.description: Sort order for returned rows. Defaults to relevance.

limit.description: Maximum businesses to return (1-50). Defaults to 20.

operations.description: Get the Google Maps or Local Finder results for one keyword searched from a coordinate. Returns each business's identity, rank, rating, categories, and hours; matching a target business in the rows is up to the caller. Uses credits. To map one business's rank across an area, use get_local_rank_grid.

keyword.description: Search query to run on Google Maps or Local Finder.

latitude.description: Latitude the SERP is fetched from.

longitude.description: Longitude the SERP is fetched from.

zoom.description: Map zoom level (4-18). Higher zoom narrows the local area. Defaults to 12, a city-sized viewport; raise it for a neighbourhood, lower it for a metro.

near.description: Coordinate (and optional map zoom) the SERP is fetched from.

searchType.description: Which local SERP to fetch. Defaults to maps.

depth.description: Number of results to fetch (1-100). Defaults to 20.

languageCode.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'vi'). Defaults to the project's default market language (see list_projects).

operations.title: Get business profile
operations.description: Get one Google Business Profile by name, cid, or placeId: categories, rating and review count, rating breakdown, address, phone, website, claimed status, opening hours, and photo count. Use it to audit the user's own profile, to compare a named competitor's, or to check whether a business has a Google Business Profile at all: it is the cheapest tool for that, at less than half the credits of search_local_businesses. Skip it when a search result already answers an identity or existence check. Uses credits. To discover businesses you cannot name yet, use search_local_businesses; for reviews and posts, use get_business_reviews and get_business_updates.

For the rating and review count alone, use get_business_profile.

Google stopped taking new questions in late 2025, so most profiles, especially small local businesses, have none. Run it only when Q&A evidence is needed. Uses credits, the same amount when nothing is found. For the profile itself, use get_business_profile.

businessName.description: Business name as it appears on Google. Supply exactly one of businessName, cid, or placeId.

operations.title: List business categories
operations.description: List Google Business categories, ranked by how many businesses use them. Use it to find valid category slugs, such as 'pizza_restaurant', for search_local_businesses; pass query to match part of a slug. Uses no credits.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against category slugs (e.g. 'plumb').

limit.description: Maximum categories to return (1-200). Defaults to 50.

operations.title: Get local rank grid
operations.description: Map how far a business's Google Maps visibility reaches: runs one Maps search per point of a square grid around a coordinate and reports where the target business ranks at each point, plus each point's result count and #1 business. Uses credits per grid point: 3x3 = 9 searches (the sensible default), 5x5 = 25. operations.title: List Search Console sites
operations.description: List the Search Console properties visible to each Google account the user has connected in the OpenSEO dashboard, and flag the one bound to the project. Use it to find the siteUrl (such as sc-domain:example.com) and accountId to pass to set_search_console_site. It cannot connect a new Google account: connectUrl is the page where the user does that. Uses no credits.

projectId.description: Required. The OpenSEO project ID to scope this call to. Get one from list_projects.

operations.title: Set project Search Console site
operations.description: Set which verified Search Console property a project reads, through a Google account the user already connected in the OpenSEO dashboard. Pass the siteUrl and gscAccountId from list_search_console_sites. Replaces the project's previous binding. Requires permission to manage integrations. Uses no credits.

operations.title: Get Google Search Console performance
operations.description: Get Google Search Console performance for the project's connected property: clicks, impressions, CTR, and average position by query, page, country, device, or date. This is first-party data: use it for what already ranks, near-ranking queries, and pages with real demand. Use minPosition, maxPosition, and minImpressions instead of fetching everything: Google can't filter by position, so they are applied server-side over the top 1000 rows by clicks. ctr is a 0-1 fraction; position is a 1-based average, omitted for type 'discover' or 'googleNews' because Google does not report it there. Dates are Pacific Time, and the last ~3 days may be incomplete. Reads only the project's connected Search Console property. Uses no credits. For a page's index status, use inspect_urls.
